greek: Εἶπεν δὲ ὁ θεὸς πρὸς Ιακωβ Ἀναστὰς ἀνάβηθι εἰς τὸν τόπον Βαιθηλ καὶ οἴκει ἐκεῖ καὶ ποίησον ἐκεῖ θυσιαστήριον τῷ θεῷ τῷ ὀφθέντι σοι ἐν τῷ ἀποδιδράσκειν σε ἀπὸ προσώπου Ησαυ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου.
hint: God tells Jacob to go up to Bethel, dwell there, and make an altar to the God who appeared to him fleeing Esau.

notes.text: ἀποδιδράσκω, *to run away*, of a slave or a fugitive; ἐν τῷ with the infinitive, the one place the article before an infinitive is printed here.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

greek: καὶ τὴν γῆν, ἣν δέδωκα Αβρααμ καὶ Ισαακ, σοὶ δέδωκα αὐτήν· σοὶ ἔσται, καὶ τῷ σπέρματί σου μετὰ σὲ δώσω τὴν γῆν ταύτην.
hint: God gives Jacob and his seed after him the land given to Abraham and Isaac.

notes.text: The perfect of δίδωμι twice over: the giving stands done, a settled state, not an act now performed.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus omits σοὶ ἔσται.

greek: ἀνέβη δὲ ὁ θεὸς ἀπʼ αὐτοῦ ἐκ τοῦ τόπου, οὗ ἐλάλησεν μετʼ αὐτοῦ.
hint: God goes up from Jacob, from the place where he spoke with him.

notes.text: ἀναβαίνω, *to go up*: the same verb as the command of 35:1, now of God himself.

greek: καὶ ἔστησεν Ιακωβ στήλην ἐν τῷ τόπῳ, ᾧ ἐλάλησεν μετʼ αὐτοῦ, στήλην λιθίνην, καὶ ἔσπεισεν ἐπʼ αὐτὴν σπονδὴν καὶ ἐπέχεεν ἐπʼ αὐτὴν ἔλαιον.
hint: Jacob sets up a stone pillar where God spoke with him, and pours a drink offering and oil on it.

notes.text: στήλη, *a block of stone*, first the thing itself and then what it marks.
σπένδω, *to pour a drink-offering*; the middle of the same verb is *to make a treaty*, since treaties were sealed by pouring.

hint: Jacob names the place where God spoke with him Bethel.

notes.text: The name is given twice in the chapter, at 35:7 and here; the Greek repeats what the Hebrew repeats.

greek: Ἀπάρας δὲ Ιακωβ ἐκ Βαιθηλ ἔπηξεν τὴν σκηνὴν αὐτοῦ ἐπέκεινα τοῦ πύργου Γαδερ. ἐγένετο δὲ ἡνίκα ἤγγισεν χαβραθα εἰς γῆν ἐλθεῖν Εφραθα, ἔτεκεν Ραχηλ καὶ ἐδυστόκησεν ἐν τῷ τοκετῷ.
hint: Leaving Bethel, Jacob camps beyond the tower of Gader; nearing Ephrath, Rachel gives birth in hard labour.

notes.text: The Hebrew kibrat, a stretch of ground of unknown length, carried into Greek untranslated; the printed page has it in lower case, where the digital module capitalises it, and the transcription follows the page.
δυστοκέω, one sense, *to be in sore travail*, said of women.

greek: ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ σκληρῶς αὐτὴν τίκτειν εἶπεν αὐτῇ ἡ μαῖα Θάρσει, καὶ γὰρ οὗτός σοί ἐστιν υἱός.
hint: The midwife bids Rachel, in her hard labour, take courage: this one too is a son.

notes.text: μαῖα, *good mother, dame* first, and *a midwife* last: the word is a form of address before it is a trade.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus omits σοί.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

hint: As her soul leaves her, Rachel names the boy 'Son of my pain'; his father calls him Benjamin.

[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus adds αὐτοῦ, *his*, marked in the Hexaplaric text with an asterisk.

greek: ἀπέθανεν δὲ Ραχηλ καὶ ἐτάφη ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ Εφραθα (αὕτη ἐστὶν Βηθλεεμ).
hint: Rachel dies and is buried on the way to Ephrath, which is Bethlehem.

notes.text: θάπτω is first *to pay the last dues to a corpse, to honour with funeral rites*, then *to bury*: the word covers the rite as well as the act.

greek: καὶ ἔστησεν Ιακωβ στήλην ἐπὶ τοῦ μνημείου αὐτῆς· αὕτη ἐστὶν στήλη μνημείου Ραχηλ ἕως τῆς σήμερον ἡμέρας.
hint: Jacob sets a pillar on Rachel's tomb, which stands there to this day.

notes.text: μνημεῖον, *a memorial*, as at 23:6: the thing that keeps the memory, before it is a grave.

greek: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἡνίκα κατῴκησεν Ισραηλ ἐν τῇ γῇ ἐκείνῃ, ἐπορεύθη Ρουβην καὶ ἐκοιμήθη μετὰ Βαλλας τῆς παλλακῆς τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ· καὶ ἤκουσεν Ισραηλ, καὶ πονηρὸν ἐφάνη ἐναντίον αὐτοῦ. Ἦσαν δὲ οἱ υἱοὶ Ιακωβ δώδεκα.
hint: Reuben sleeps with his father's concubine Bilhah, and Israel hears and takes it ill. Jacob's sons are twelve.

notes.text: The neuter as a noun with φαίνω: a toilsome thing appeared, where the Hebrew says simply that Israel heard.

notes.lemma: Ἦσαν δὲ οἱ υἱοὶ Ιακωβ δώδεκα
notes.text: The sentence stands in the same verse as Reuben's act, with nothing between them: the twelve are counted where the offence is told.

greek: υἱοὶ Λειας· πρωτότοκος Ιακωβ Ρουβην, Συμεων, Λευι, Ιουδας, Ισσαχαρ, Ζαβουλων.
hint: Leah's six sons, from Reuben the firstborn to Zebulun.

notes.text: πρωτότοκος, *firstborn*, the word that carries the whole of Genesis's quarrel over birthright.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus reads Λευεις.

reading: sons of [[name:Λειας]]; first-born of [[name:Ιακωβ]] [[name:Ρουβην]], [[name:Συμεων]], [[name:Λευι]], [[name:Ιουδας]], [[name:Ισσαχαρ]], [[name:Ζαβουλων]].

names.gloss: (Λεια, from Hebrew Lēʾâ, of uncertain meaning, perhaps "wild cow")
(Συμεων, from Hebrew Šimʿôn, which the Hebrew of 29:33 hears in šāmaʿ, "he heard")
(Λευι, from Hebrew Lēwî, which the Hebrew of 29:34 hears in lāwâ, "he was joined")
(Ιουδας, from Hebrew Yĕhûdâ, which the Hebrew of 29:35 hears in yādâ, "to praise")
(Ισσαχαρ, from Hebrew Yiśśāśkār, which the Hebrew of 30:18 hears in śākār, "wages")
(Ζαβουλων, from Hebrew Zĕbûlûn, which the Hebrew of 30:20 hears in zābal, "to dwell with honour")

greek: υἱοὶ δὲ Ραχηλ· Ιωσηφ καὶ Βενιαμιν.
hint: Rachel's two sons, Joseph and Benjamin.

notes.text: The list runs without a verb throughout 35:23-26: the Greek keeps the Hebrew's bare naming.

reading: sons [[but|but, while / whereas / on the other hand, then / yet, at, I say / now / so then|δέ]], of [[name:Ραχηλ]]; [[name:Ιωσηφ]] and [[name:Βενιαμιν]].

names.gloss: (Ιωσηφ, from Hebrew Yôsēp̄, which the Hebrew of 30:24 hears in yōsēp̄, "may he add")

greek: υἱοὶ δὲ Βαλλας παιδίσκης Ραχηλ· Δαν καὶ Νεφθαλι.
hint: Bilhah's two sons, Dan and Naphtali.

notes.text: [[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus reads Νεφθαλειμ.

reading: sons [[but|but, while / whereas / on the other hand, then / yet, at, I say / now / so then|δέ]], of [[name:Βαλλας]] [[of a young girl|of a young girl / maiden, of a young slave / courtesan|παιδίσκη]] of [[name:Ραχηλ]]; [[name:Δαν]] and [[name:Νεφθαλι]].

names.gloss: (Δαν, from Hebrew Dān, which the Hebrew of 30:6 hears in dîn, "he judged")
(Νεφθαλι, from Hebrew Naptālî, which the Hebrew of 30:8 hears in niptal, "I have wrestled")

greek: υἱοὶ δὲ Ζελφας παιδίσκης Λειας· Γαδ καὶ Ασηρ. οὗτοι υἱοὶ Ιακωβ, οἳ ἐγένοντο αὐτῷ ἐν Μεσοποταμίᾳ τῆς Συρίας.
hint: Zilpah's two sons, Gad and Asher; these are Jacob's sons, born to him in Mesopotamia of Syria.

notes.text: [[flag]] All twelve are said to have been born in Mesopotamia, though Benjamin was born at Ephrath in 35:16-18; the Hebrew says the same.

reading: sons [[but|but, while / whereas / on the other hand, then / yet, at, I say / now / so then|δέ]], of [[name:Ζελφας]] [[of a young girl|of a young girl / maiden, of a young slave / courtesan|παιδίσκη]] of [[name:Λειας]]; [[name:Γαδ]] and [[name:Ασηρ]]. [[these|these, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] sons of [[name:Ιακωβ]], which [[came into being|there came to be, there arose, there was brought into existence|γίνομαι]] to him [[in|within, inside of, and by means of|ἐν]] to [[name:Μεσοποταμίᾳ]] of the [[name:Συρίας]].

names.gloss: (Ζελφα, from Hebrew Zilpâ, of uncertain meaning)
(Γαδ, from Hebrew Gād, which the Hebrew of 30:11 hears in gād, "fortune")
(Ασηρ, from Hebrew ʾĀšēr, which the Hebrew of 30:13 hears in ʾōšer, "happiness")

greek: Ἦλθεν δὲ Ιακωβ πρὸς Ισαακ τὸν πατέρα αὐτοῦ εἰς Μαμβρη εἰς πόλιν τοῦ πεδίου (αὕτη ἐστὶν Χεβρων) ἐν γῇ Χανααν, οὗ παρῴκησεν Αβρααμ καὶ Ισαακ.
hint: Jacob comes to his father Isaac at Mamre, which is Hebron, where Abraham and Isaac sojourned.

notes.text: παροικέω, *to dwell beside*, of a resident alien: neither man ever owned the land he lived in.

reading: [[came|came / went, came / went back / returned|ἔρχομαι]] [[but|but, while / whereas / on the other hand, then / yet, at, I say / now / so then|δέ]], [[name:Ιακωβ]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] [[name:Ισαακ]] [[the father|the father, the grandfather|πατήρ]] of him [[into|into / to, into or to, in, rest in, there, to / up to / until, till, against, for a, at, on, with, as far as, as much as, to the number of, to or towards, in regard to|εἰς]] [[name:Μαμβρη]] [[into|into / to, into or to, in, rest in, there, to / up to / until, till, against, for a, at, on, with, as far as, as much as, to the number of, to or towards, in regard to|εἰς]] [[city|city, citadel, one's city / country, body of citizens, a number of citizens, state, a free state / republic, the right of citizenship|πόλις]] [[of the plain|of the plain / flat, of the plain flat open country|πεδίον]] ([[this|this, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] is [[name:Χεβρων]]) [[in|within, inside of, and by means of|ἐν]] [[to earth|to earth, to land, to a land / country, to the earth / ground, to a lump of earth|γῆ]] of [[name:Χανααν]], where [[dwelt beside|dwelt beside, dwelt along the coast of, lived near, dwelt among, lay near, lived in and sojourned|παροικέω]] [[name:Αβρααμ]] and [[name:Ισαακ]].

names.gloss: (Μαμβρη, from Hebrew Mamrēʾ, of uncertain meaning)
(Χεβρων, from Hebrew Ḥebrôn, usually connected with ḥābar, "to join")

greek: ἐγένοντο δὲ αἱ ἡμέραι Ισαακ, ἃς ἔζησεν, ἔτη ἑκατὸν ὀγδοήκοντα·
hint: Isaac lives a hundred and eighty years.

notes.text: ζάω, *to live*, with the days as its object: the Greek counts the days he lived, not the years he was.

reading: [[came into being|there came to be, there arose, there was brought into existence|γίνομαι]] [[but|but, while / whereas / on the other hand, then / yet, at, I say / now / so then|δέ]], [[the days|the days, the states / times of life|ἡμέρα]] of [[name:Ισαακ]], which [[lived|lived, lived off or on, was in full life / strength / fresh and strong|ζάω]], years hundred eighty;

greek: καὶ ἐκλιπὼν ἀπέθανεν καὶ προσετέθη πρὸς τὸ γένος αὐτοῦ πρεσβύτερος καὶ πλήρης ἡμερῶν, καὶ ἔθαψαν αὐτὸν Ησαυ καὶ Ιακωβ οἱ υἱοὶ αὐτοῦ.
hint: Isaac dies at a great age and is added to his kin; his sons Esau and Jacob bury him.

notes.text: ἐκλείπω, *to leave out*, and so *to fail, die away*: the Greek says he left off before it says he died.
προστίθημι in the passive, *was put to*: the dead man is added to his kin, as at 25:8 and 25:17.

reading: and [[having left out|having left out / omitted / passed over, having forsaken / deserted / abandoned, having suffered an eclipse, having died, having left off / ceased / stopped, having failed / been wanting|ἐκλείπω]] [[died off|died off / died, was ready to die, was put to death / slain|ἀποθνήσκω]] and [[was put to|was put to, was handed over / delivered, was given / bestowed, was imposed further, was attributed / imputed to, was added, was joined|προστίθημι]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] [[the race|the race / stock / family, the offspring / posterity, the single descendant / child, the clan / house, the tribe and caste, the breed, the age / generation, the age / time of life, the sex and gender, the class / sort / kind, the genus|γένος]] of him [[elder|elder, elder / older, higher / more important, greater than, elders of the Jewish Council, elders of the Church / presbyters|πρεσβύτερος]] and [[full|full, filled / infected by, satiated with, full of people, full / complete|πλήρης]] [[of days|of days, of states / times of life|ἡμέρα]], and [[paid the last dues to a corpse|paid the last dues to a corpse / honoured with funeral rites, buried / interred|θάπτω]] him [[name:Ησαυ]] and [[name:Ιακωβ]] the sons of him.
